properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP-0038 encrypted private keys (WIF): live AES-256-ECB chains in Key encrypt/decrypt paths (non-EC and EC-multiplied), PyCryptodome cipher. ECB is fixed by the BIP38 spec for interoperability — changeable only by deviating from the spec. Quantum exposure is Grover-only at the 256-bit key.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Implements the OP_SHA1 Bitcoin Script opcode: SHA-1 digest of the top stack item, executed when a script runs OP_SHA1. The algorithm is fixed by the Bitcoin script protocol — observable here, replaceable only by Bitcoin consensus, not by this library. Collision-broken as a general hash but used here purely as a script opcode, not for any integrity decision of the library itself.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Derives the AES-SIV database field-encryption key from the DB_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD environment variable: unsalted double-SHA-256 (fast digest) instead of a password KDF — a captured database is offline-brute-forceable at password-guessing speed. The codebase already ships scrypt (encoding.scrypt_hash); alternatively DB_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY accepts a raw 32-byte hex key and skips the derivation entirely. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Bitcoin protocol's curve, used everywhere in the library: domain parameters in config/secp256k1.py, modular key arithmetic and EC point operations in keys.py (fastecdsa native path + python-ecdsa fallback), range checks in mnemonic.py, and matching test coverage. This is a blockchain-curve asset: a Bitcoin library cannot unilaterally substitute ML-DSA — the curve is decided by Bitcoin network governance, observable here, replaceable only network-wide.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP39 mnemonic-to-seed derivation: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations, salt b'mnemonic'+passphrase. The iteration count is fixed by the BIP39 standard — raising it would break seed compatibility with every other BIP39 wallet, so it is not tunable in practice. 2048 sits far below OWASP's password-storage guidance, but the secret input here is a 128–256-bit entropy-encoded mnemonic rather than a human password, so offline brute-force economics are those of guessing the mnemonic itself.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Encrypted wallet database: when a password is supplied, Db.__init__ builds a sqlite+pysqlcipher URI (requires pysqlcipher3) selecting cipher=aes-256-cfb with kdf_iter=64000. CFB is an unauthenticated block-cipher mode as such (SQLCipher layers its own page-level HMAC, which mitigates malleability); the weaker, tunable parameter is kdf_iter=64000 — the SQLCipher v3 default, raised to 256000 in v4. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Bitcoin transaction/message signatures: fastecdsa native path (_ecdsa.sign, get_public_key) with python-ecdsa fallback (SigningKey.from_string/sign_digest), RFC6979 deterministic nonces (both libraries), VerifyingKey verification, DER encoding; setup.cfg:42 declares the ecdsa dependency for Windows; test files cover RFC6979 signing. Classical signature, Shor-vulnerable — but the signature scheme is fixed by the Bitcoin protocol; ML-DSA-style migration is a network-governance decision, observable

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 across the whole Bitcoin stack: double-SHA256 for transaction/block hashes, hash160 for address derivation, BIP39 checksum, Script OP_SHA256/OP_HASH256 opcodes, RFC6979 deterministic nonces and ECDSA signature digest, plus testnet service helper and RFC6979 test vectors. Grover gives only a square-root speedup, and the uses are protocol-fixed; quantum-safe for practical purposes.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: aes_encrypt/aes_decrypt helpers in encoding.py: AES with 32-byte key in SIV mode (RFC 5297 synthetic-IV, deterministic, nonce-misuse-resistant AEAD) — used by db.py's EncryptedBinary type to encrypt wallet database fields. Strong posture, nothing to migrate; note the docstring's "AES-128" mention is inaccurate — a 32-byte key means AES-256.
